children: A reverse-reference lookup that answers "what breaks if I delete or unpublish this?" — the first Graph View surface shipped in LiveView Studio.

Blast Radius queries the Content Edges Table by to_id to find every Document that references the one you're about to delete or unpublish. Before the destructive Mutation commits, Studio shows the operator exactly which documents would acquire a Dangling Reference — i.e. which downstream content would suddenly point at a Phantom Node.

A single Reference Field can be arrayOf, holding many targets. Blast Radius uses the reverse_referencers helper so that a referrer is counted once per real edge regardless of whether the link came from a scalar reference or one slot of an array. This is the same helper Graph Traversal uses for reverse expansion, so the two stay consistent.

consumer of the materialized graph in LiveView Studio — it predates the full Graph View pane and proved the Edge Projector → Content Edges Table pipeline end to end. It is a focused, single-question slice of what the Graph Renderer later visualizes wholesale.

It turns a quiet referential-integrity hazard into an explicit, pre-commit decision. The FK on content_edges stops a stored edge from dangling, but only Blast Radius warns a human before they create the dangle by removing a target. The lookup is also exposed headlessly under /v1/graph on the HTTP API v1, so any Surfaces client can ask "what references this?" before deleting.
